classification.description: The world’s fastest framework for building websites.

plan.architecture_summary: Hugo is a high-performance static site generator written in Go, organized into domain-specific packages such as hugolib (core site building and rendering), commands (CLI interface), markup (Markdown processing via Goldmark), and resources (asset pipelines and file management). The main entry point is main.go, which wires up the command-line interface and delegates building and rendering tasks to hugolib and other subpackages. Testing is heavily driven by Go's standard test framework, integration test scripts, and Mage (via magefile.go).

commit: Imperative mood starting with a capital letter and no trailing period for commit subjects.
Prefix commits with the package name (e.g. `media: Add text/calendar`), functional topic, or `all:` / `docs:`.
Reference issues with `Fixes #1234` or `See #1234` in the commit body.
pull_request: Include test cases for new code.
Add documentation in `/docs` if adding new features or changing functionality.
Squash commits into a single commit before final review.

issues.title: Include default gitignore in project generator.
issues.why: Well-scoped feature request touching the commands package with straightforward Go file creation.
issues.approach: Examine `commands/new.go` and site generator logic to generate a default `.gitignore` file alongside other site skeleton files when `hugo new site` / `hugo new project` runs. Add corresponding test coverage.

issues.title: Warn when a folder contains both index.md and _index.md (silent content loss)
issues.why: Clear enhancement proposal with a concrete diagnostic goal that fits a beginner Go developer looking at content loading.
issues.approach: Inspect `hugolib` or configuration logic to add a warning message when a content directory contains both `index.md` and `_index.md`. Add unit/integration tests to verify the warning triggers correctly.

issues.title: Specify parameters via command line (env not portable)
issues.why: Improves developer experience across platforms (Windows/Linux) by exposing command-line options in the commands package.
issues.approach: Investigate `commands/env.go` or command-line flag parsing to support specifying user parameters via command-line flags rather than exclusively via environment variables. Add tests for flag-based parameter overrides.

issues.title: Support document-oriented XML in transform.Unmarshal
issues.why: Great stretching task for a Go beginner interested in data transformation and parsing in the transform package.
issues.approach: Inspect how `transform.Unmarshal` handles XML data structures and check if document-oriented XML decoding can be supported or configured using standard Go XML parsers or options. Add test cases with Doxygen-like XML samples.

first_timer_insights: First-time contributor PRs are typically small, focused bug fixes or feature additions in packages like markup, resources, or documentation/AGENTS.md.
They include dedicated unit or integration tests in the same package (e.g., xxx_integration_test.go).
They follow strict package-prefixed commit message conventions and pass CI checks cleanly.
caveats: No pull request template file was present in the repository.
Contributor License Agreement (CLA) must be signed via CLA-assistant on first PR.
